text:
Connor Hellebuyck's first season in New Jersey has come with more weight than most. He asked out of Winnipeg, and this month he explained why, in a story Yahoo Sports headlined "Hellebuyck: Threats Against Family Went Beyond Online Death Threats." On Saturday in St. Louis he was pulled after a first period CBS Sports called disastrous, in a 9-6 loss. We have him projected back in net tonight against Columbus, at .897 and 0.7 goals below expected through nine games, after finishing 3.43 above expected over 57 games last season.

The strange part is how good the Devils' game is in front of him. They take 57% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and their goal difference is +14 on +22.3 expected. Goaltending, 9.6 goals allowed above expected as a team, is the leak; even St. Louis was theirs on chances. Anthony Mantha (neck) and Johnathan Kovacevic are out; Cody Glass has taken Mantha's spot beside Evan Rodrigues, who has eight points in his last ten and is one of our Sleepers.

Columbus arrives feeling better. Down two goals in Toronto on Saturday, the Blue Jackets came back to win 4-3, their second straight, with Matthew Knies back in the building he left in the preseason trade for Kirill Marchenko. Zach Werenski has 11 points in his last ten and goals in three straight, and Kent Johnson has a five-game point streak. His name keeps turning up in trade talk, though Yahoo Sports reports he remains committed. Sean Monahan is still out, with Adam Fantilli in his spot beside Valeri Nichushkin.

The standings explain the stakes. Columbus is seventh in the Metropolitan, twelve points behind second-place New Jersey, and our numbers give the Jackets a 9% playoff chance to the Devils' 94%. Tonight we have New Jersey at 3.72 expected goals and Columbus at 2.78, the first half of a home-and-home Mike Fink of The Hockey News called pivotal. Jet Greaves (.875) is projected for Columbus, and Mathieu Olivier sits one goal from 50 for his career.
headline: After nine in St. Louis, Devils host Columbus
